image_description: A single Rock Beauty angelfish (Holocanthus tricolor) swimming in a marine environment. The fish displays the characteristic black anterior body and head, transitioning to a golden yellow posterior body and tail. It is positioned near coral structures, with a brain coral visible in the lower left.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fish exhibits the classic high-bodied, laterally compressed shape typical of angelfish/butterflyfish.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Striking gold and black coloration: anterior body and head black, posterior body and tail golden yellow with black margin.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The color pattern matches the species description perfectly: black front half, yellow back half. A dark margin on the tail is faintly visible/consistent with the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal fin is continuous along the back. While individual spines vs rays are hard to distinguish at this resolution, the structural continuity is correct.
The anal fin is visible on the ventral side, mirroring the dorsal fin's position and general shape.
The caudal fin appears rounded, consistent with the species morphology.

To ensure the fins are properly connected to the body and there is no 'melting' into the background water, which is common in aquatic AI generations.
